source.exp: Conduction transfers thermal energy through molecular/electronic interactions without bulk transport of matter. Direct contact between bodies is one common situation, but conduction also occurs within a single body.

source.q: Can liquids transfer heat by conduction?
source.a: Yes; conduction can occur in liquids, although convection is often also important.
source.exp: Liquids do conduct heat; the textbook habit of associating conduction with solids refers to dominance, not exclusivity. Mercury is not the only conducting liquid.

source.q: What happens to an ordinary gravity pendulum inside an orbiting spacecraft in ideal weightlessness?
source.a: It does not execute ordinary pendulum oscillations because the effective restoring gravity is essentially zero.
source.exp: A simple pendulum needs gravity to provide a restoring component. In ideal free fall, effective gravity in the spacecraft is approximately zero, so ordinary pendulum SHM does not occur; writing T → ∞ is only a formal limit of the formula.

source.q: Why does a simple pendulum fail to oscillate normally in ideal orbital weightlessness?
source.a: Because there is essentially no effective gravitational restoring force on the bob relative to the spacecraft.
source.exp: The bob and support are both in free fall. With essentially no effective gravity to create a restoring component, the pendulum does not perform ordinary gravity-driven oscillations.
